title: Real-time machine learning is associated with fewer weeks of inpatient hypoglycemia
summary: A previously validated gradient-boosted model predicting inpatient hypoglycemia was implemented on a cardiovascular and vascular surgery ward. Across 3,989 pre-implementation and 1,916 post-implementation hospitalizations, more than 5% of patients had hypoglycemia in 9.4% of weeks (12/127) before versus 0% (0/79) after implementation (p=0.012). The design is a non-randomized pre/post comparison on one ward and may be confounded. Preprint of 2022-07-24.
ai_technology: Supervised machine learning (extreme gradient boosting) predicting inpatient hypoglycemia from medications, labs and clinical data
organization: Sinai Health System; Unity Health Toronto

evidence.tested: Prospective pre/post implementation analysis of the deployed model on 3,989 pre- and 1,916 post-implementation hospitalizations.
evidence.unknown: Causal effect of the model, generalizability beyond one ward and peer-reviewed status are not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deployed machine learning model predicted hypoglycemia risk to support prevention.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations were not available. Publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
